item.title: ICELANDERS OF SPRING RIDGE — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Fred Bjarnason Victoria, British Columbia, was a very different place when Icelanders began to settle here in 1883 than it is now. The city followed the waterfront along the inner harbour, extending inland only about four or five blocks. The Icelanders began to settle in an area east of the main city known as Spring Ridge, now the neighbour of Fernwood. item.title: Markerville…Small and Proud — Icelandic Roots
item.description: by Shaune Jonasson As we explore the Icelandic settlements in Alberta, one particular area comes to mind. Markerville began as a small community and has remained relatively small over these many years. However, despite its size, it is no less important than any other Icelandic settlement in North America. Its footprint is as impressive today as it ever has been. item.title: My Time as Fjallkona — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Alfreda Duffy The Lady of the Mountain (Fjallkona) is the female incarnation, or national personification, of Iceland.1 The concept of a Fjallkona was first introduced in a poem by Ofsjónir við jarðarför Lovísu drottningar 1752 (Visions at the funeral of Queen Louise, 1752) by Eggert Ólafsson. The image described in this poem no longer exists. It wasn’t until 1866, when a poem titled Eldgamla Ísafold by Bjarni Thorarensen was published in a book of Icelandic folktales and symbols...

item.title: Stephan G. Stephansson: Interesting Icelander for November 2026 — Icelandic Roots
item.description: Stephan G. Stephansson was an Icelandic-born poet, farmer, and community leader whose life spanned two continents. Born in northern Iceland in 1853, he emigrated to North America in search of a better life. After settling first in Wisconsin and then in North Dakota, he moved to Alberta in 1889. Writing in Icelandic, he became one of the most prolific poets of his time. Photo sourced through the IcelandicRoots.com database. item.title: Book Club for November 2026 — Icelandic Roots
item.description: by Gayle Graham It is a pleasure to invite you to the November 5th Icelandic Roots Book Club to hear from Cathie Eliasson, the author of Falcons Forever: the Saga of the 1920 Olympic Gold Medal Ice Hockey Team.
